_info: ClimaCredit Q v6 - all assumptions in one place. Change a value here and the notebook, the quantum model and the server all use it. Each entry has a value and a source.

bank_size_meur.source: Assumption: corporate loan book of a typical local OP cooperative bank (a few hundred MEUR).

lgd.source: Basel foundation IRB LGD for senior unsecured corporate exposures.

rho_economy.source: Basel corporate asset correlation range 0.12-0.24. Finnish bankruptcy data alone give only about 0.01 (see notebook), but bank capital is set with the Basel range, so the price of capital uses it.

rho_climate.source: Assumption: agriculture and construction are the most climate-sensitive sectors (ECB 2022 climate stress test). For farm loans the value is scaled per region by how much the local harvest swings (Eurostat 2010-2024).

flood_rho_add.source: Assumption: extra climate sensitivity in regions with a significant RIVER flood risk area (fields and towns along the river).

coastal_flood_rho_add.source: Assumption: extra climate sensitivity in regions with a significant COASTAL (sea) flood risk area (buildings, ports and shops, not fields).

flood_areas.source: The 18 significant flood risk areas 2025-2030 (14 river, 4 coastal), Ministry of Agriculture and Forestry decision 19.12.2024 and the regional ELY centre proposals. Loviisa, Riihimäki, Lapua and Kemijärvi were dropped from the 2018 list.

pd_agriculture_national.source: Starting PD of EU banks' agricultural loans, ECB/ESAs Fit-for-55 climate scenario analysis (Nov 2024). Finnish farm bankruptcies (about 0.08 % a year) are far too rare to measure bank defaults, so agriculture gets its own EU anchor.

pd_construction_trade_average.source: Average PD of EU banks' corporate loans, ECB/ESAs Fit-for-55 (Nov 2024). The average of construction and trade loans is set to this level; Finnish defaults (bankruptcies + restructurings, Statistics Finland 2018-2024) decide how it splits between the two sectors and across regions.

pd_scale_construction_trade.source: Extra multiplier on the calibrated construction and trade PD (1.0 = as calibrated). Kept so you can stress the level.

regional_weight.source: How much regional differences in bankruptcy rates count (0 = same PD everywhere, 1 = full credibility-weighted difference).

credibility_k.source: Credibility weighting: a region's own bankruptcy rate gets the weight n/(n+k), where n = its bankruptcies 2018-2024. Small regions are pulled towards the national rate (actuarial Bühlmann credibility).

drought_regional_weight.source: How much of the regional difference in harvest volatility we use (0 = none, 1 = all). Only 15 years of regional harvest data (Eurostat 2010-2024), so we use half.

scenarios.source: Average corporate PD rises from 2.4% by +0.6 / +1.3 / +2.3 p.p. to 2030, ECB/ESAs Fit-for-55 climate scenario analysis (Nov 2024). These are averages over all sectors.

main_scenario.source: Choice: the disorderly transition scenario of Fit-for-55.

transition_sector_tilt.source: How much the transition shock differs between sectors (0 = all sectors get the EU average, 1 = full pattern of the 2022 energy crisis, when farm bankruptcies rose 31 % and construction 16 % more than the whole economy and trade not at all). 0.5 because the energy crisis also overlapped with rate hikes and a housing slump.

weather_years.source: Historical analogue years for physical climate risk. 2019: best harvest relative to trend in 2010-2024 (about +20 %). 2018: drought, farm entrepreneurial income fell almost 40 % (Luke). 2021: hot, dry summer and the smallest cereal harvest since 1992 (Luke, FMI). Regional harvest deviations from Eurostat (apro_cpnhr), 2010-2024.

weather_beta.source: Farm PD multiplier = exp(-beta x harvest deviation from trend). beta = 1.5: a harvest 25 % below trend gives about 1.5 x the farm defaults. Single events suggest 1.7-1.9 (2021: harvest -25 % and farm bankruptcies +78 %, partly a rebound after the 2020 bankruptcy freeze; 2018: farm entrepreneurial income -40 %, Luke); a regression over all years finds a weaker link. Illustrative - few events.

bank_margin.source: The bank's own margin, which already covers today's credit risk and costs. Adjustable per loan in the app.

euribor_fallback.source: Euribor monthly averages Sep 2026 (ECB / EMMI), used only if the live ECB feed is unavailable.

cost_of_capital.source: Assumption: required return on the bank's equity used to price the extra capital a loan needs.

firm_adjustment.source: Assumption: PD multiplier from the firm's key ratios relative to the sector average.

equity_ratio_limits.source: Finnish Yritystutkimus standard: equity ratio >40% strong, 20-40% satisfactory, <20% weak.

net_debt_ebitda_limits.source: Bank rule of thumb: net debt/EBITDA <3 strong, 3-5 satisfactory, >5 weak.

subindustry_prior_strength.source: Empirical Bayes shrinkage of sub-industry risk (TOL 3-digit, bankruptcies 2019-2024): a sub-industry with few bankruptcies is pulled towards its sector. At least 5 expected bankruptcies' worth of prior.
